conviction_note: Findings roughly offset (rate tailwind and a possible NII guide nudge against a Spanish-bank results season in which in-line prints were sold hard and stretched valuation), so impact_sum is -0.1; abs_move 4.5 because the quarter is not pre-released, a further NII guide change is plausible and sector peers moved 4-8% on their own Q3 prints this month, and p_up 48 because nothing company-level and unpublished decides the sign; print_vs_bar (+3, weak, bar unsourced at quarter level) leans positive while the reaction function this season leans negative, which is why the two disagree.

already_public.what: Release date: OIR of 22 Sep 2026 says Unicaja presents Q3 2026 results on 30 Oct 2026 at 11:00 CET (webcast + Q&A).

2026 guidance updated (raised) with H1: NII +Low-Mid SD (was >2025), fees +LSD, costs +MSD, cost of risk 20-25bp (was <30bp), net profit +MSD (was >2025); payout 95%, all cash in three payments (Sep, Dec 2026, Apr 2027); H1 net profit 361m (+7.1%), Q2 NII 382m (+2.3% QoQ), CET1 15.8%.
FY2026 market consensus net profit EUR 630m as cited by the company (used for its 2026E dividend yield).
Chairman José Sevilla will not seek re-election when his mandate ends in April 2027.

possible nudge of 2026 NII guide from +Low-Mid SD toward +MSD and/or net profit guide; unknown, mild upside skew
December additional remuneration (c.25% of profit, cash) likely quantified; inside the stated policy, expected neutral
chairman succession may be commented on; not expected to move the stock

findings.finding: The ECB hiked in June (deposit rate 2.25%) and September 2026 (2.50%), and 12m Euribor averaged 2.86/2.95/3.25% in Jul/Aug/Sep against ~2.80% in Q2, a tailwind to Unicaja's Euribor-linked mortgage book that the July guide (NII +Low-Mid SD) only partly embedded, giving scope for Q3 NII growth and a further NII-guide nudge; offset in part by deposit costs, which the company said rose in Q2 'mainly explained [by the] ECB rate hike'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (31 Jul 2026), when the 2026 guide was raised across NII, CoR and net profit, the stock rose +2.2% against IBEX +0.1% (Yahoo daily bars); Q1 2026 reiterated guide, +1.4% vs IBEX +1.8%.
findings.original_quote: Septiembre 2026 3,247% ... Agosto 2026 2,954% ... Julio 2026 2,855% ... Junio 2026 2,798% (medias mensuales del Euríbor 12 meses); presentation: 'Deposits: Higher cost mainly explained ECB rate hike'
findings.why_not_priced: The rate path is public, so most of this is in the price; what is not is Unicaja's own translation of it into the 2026 NII guide, which only the release will carry. If the market had priced a guide raise, UNI would not be down 5.9% over 20 days and 9.1% over 60 days with targets clustered at or below spot.
findings.independence: ECB hikes: https://www.raisin.com/es-es/ahorro/decision-tipos-de-interes-bce/ (separate source for the policy path); company's Q2 slide on NII bridge (https://www.unicajabanco.com/content/dam/unicaja/unicaja-corporacion/documentos-corporacion/inversores-y-accionistas/presentacion-unicaja-2T26.pdf) is the counterweight on deposit costs.

findings.finding: Spanish bank Q3 2026 prints are being sold even when in line: Bankinter reported 9M net profit of EUR 901m (+11%) with NII in line with consensus on 22 Oct and fell 7.56%, dragging CaixaBank -5.72% and Santander -4.06% (UNI -4.0% that day), and analysts framed it as NII having peaked; Santander then fell 5.6% on 28 Oct, its scheduled Q3 day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UNI's own last six results days moved +3.5, -0.9, -0.4, +2.6, +1.4, +2.2% (real release dates, Yahoo bars): it has not systematically sold its prints, which is why this is sized small rather than as a veto.
findings.original_quote: Renta 4: 'Bankinter cuente con una reacción negativa de la cotización al mostrar unas cifras sin sorpresas'
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: UNI fell with the sector on 22 Oct. What is not priced is the reaction function on UNI's own day; if the market had already discounted a sold print, UNI's 5-day run-up would not be +2.3% back toward pre-Bankinter levels (3.20 vs 3.25 on 21 Oct).
findings.independence: Index-level confirmation of the 22 Oct drop and Bankinter -7.56%: https://www.articulo14.es/economia/ibex-35-bajo-19000-puntos-20261022.html ; Santander's 28 Oct Q3 date: https://capital.com/en-gb/market-updates/santander-share-price-forecast-05-08-2026 (move from Yahoo bars, cause inferred).

findings.finding: Sell-side is cautious on valuation with spot (EUR 3.20) at or above dated targets: Deutsche Bank raised its target to EUR 3.25 but kept Hold, warning 'las acciones parecen cada vez más caras' (6 Aug 2026), and Citi is Neutral at EUR 3.33 (15 Sep 2026), so a merely in-line quarter has little multiple support.

findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced (it is broker copy); kept small because it shapes the reaction to an in-line print rather than the print itself.

findings.finding: The December 2026 additional remuneration (c.25% of profit, cash, per the 2026 plan of 95% total payout in three cash payments) is likely to be quantified in this release, with CET1 at 15.8% and a EUR 2.2bn CET1 buffer behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026 release raised the interim dividend 28% and the stock rose 2.2%; mixed with the guidance raise that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside the stated policy, so near zero; only a buyback or an amount above 25% would be new, and the H1 release said 2026 is paid 'íntegramente en efectivo'.
